topic.title: Deployment Architecture Overview
topic.shortdesc: A high-level overview of the on-premises deployment architecture, including supported clients, authentication options, and sizing guidance.

body.p: The solution is delivered as a self-contained Linux installer. The entire platform runs as containers on a single Linux host (a virtual machine or physical server that you control). The components communicate over an isolated internal network on that host, and only a small, well-defined set of ports is exposed externally.

section.title: Solution Architecture
section.p: All services run on a single Linux host. The web tier terminates HTTPS and proxies requests to the core platform services, which use bundled PostgreSQL and Redis instances. Outbound integrations are optional and can be disabled, so the deployment is capable of running fully air-gapped.

image.alt: Browsers and Oxygen XML Author connect over HTTPS to a Content Fusion server running on a single Linux host. The server includes an NGINX web tier, core platform services, PostgreSQL, and cache. Optional outbound integrations include SMTP, LDAP or Active Directory, OIDC SSO, Git, and AI providers.

section.p: Users connect to through two supported clients:

dlentry.dd: The primary client for reviewers, authors, and administrators. The review UI runs in any modern web browser over HTTPS, so the end-user operating system is unconstrained.

The installed desktop application on author workstations connects to through its built-in Oxygen Content Fusion Connector add-on over HTTPS to submit documents for review and retrieve feedback. The desktop client is installed and licensed independently and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

section.title: Technology Stack
section.p: All run times and infrastructure components below are bundled inside the delivered container images. You do not install or separately maintain a Java runtime, application server, or database on the host (only a supported operating system and a container engine are required).

row.entry: Docker containers on Linux, orchestrated with Docker Compose

section.note: A full inventory of bundled components and their versions (SBOM) is available on request for vulnerability scanning and compliance.

section.title: Hardware Sizing Guidance
section.p: The workload is driven primarily by publishing/validation batch jobs (CPU-intensive) and active review sessions (memory-intensive), more than by raw connection count.

ul.li: Storage grows with the number and size of review tasks, document revisions, published outputs, and the search index. Provision generously and monitor it, and an SSD is strongly recommended. For details about how storage is used and how to add more, see and .
Publishing is the heaviest CPU consumer. Sites that publish large DITA maps frequently should favor more CPUs.
For deployments that need more memory allocated to the services, see .

section.title: Network and Ports
section.p: Inbound access is over HTTPS on port 443 (browsers, the desktop Author connector, and Web Author), with port 80 typically redirecting to HTTPS.
Port 9080 serves the administration console (restrict this to administrator networks).
For the external services that must be reachable when the corresponding features are enabled, see .
For the authoritative list of incoming and outgoing connections, see .

ul.li: [Recommended] OIDC single sign-on (for example, Microsoft Entra ID or Okta)

section.title: Backup, High Availability, and Dependencies
section.p: The appliance includes built-in backup tooling (shell scripts that save the backup locally). Integrate the backups into your organization's standard backup rotation and storage, and test restores periodically. For the backup and restore procedure, see .
